core.title: Give each journey spec well-formed test URNs naming its own subject
core.given: A journey spec: a file of the end-to-end test kind that the stack's end-to-end test runner actually runs, or any test-kind file whose header comments carry a journey binding marker (the stack's train or journey binding syntax).
core.when: The spec is written or changed.
core.then: It carries at least one test URN in the stack's test URN shape, and every URN it carries is well-formed and names the subject its binding header declares.
prefer: The same test URN in the spec's header and its test title.
The harness code in the URN matching the kind of test the spec exercises.
avoid: Malformed URNs (wrong prefix, unknown harness code, missing sequence number or slug).
URNs naming a different train/journey than this spec's binding.
Renaming a spec away from the end-to-end test kind's naming pattern to dodge the check; the header binding markers still apply.
unless: Vendored or generated trees (the stack's never-scanned excluded roots).
A malformed binding header: no URN-vs-binding comparison is made (URN format is still checked); the companion binding-header rule alone reports the malformed binding.
core.why: The URN identifies the test instance and its harness. A malformed URN, or one naming another subject, silently traces the result to the wrong place.
evidence: The stack's journey-URN check reports no finding for the spec.
Every journey spec carries at least one URN matching the stack's test URN shape, and each URN's train/journey id equals the subject of its valid binding header.
verification: Journey-spec recognition: a file of the end-to-end test kind that the stack's end-to-end test runner runs (the runner's own test-set membership establishes this, not the file name; an observer may be needed), or any test-kind file whose header comments carry a train/journey binding marker — so misnamed specs are still judged. A test that merely mentions a journey URN inside a string literal is not a journey spec.

URN check against the stack's test URN shape: at least one URN per journey spec, and every URN the spec carries must match; wrong prefix, unknown harness code, malformed sequence number or missing slug is a finding.
Never scan the stack's excluded (vendored and generated) trees.
Compare a URN's subject with its binding only when the binding is valid; a malformed binding is reported solely by the companion binding-header rule — no duplicate finding here.

fires: A file of the end-to-end test kind that the stack's end-to-end test runner runs is added or edited and carries no test URN.
A journey spec carries a URN with an unknown harness code, a malformed sequence number, or no slug.
A test-kind file that does not follow the end-to-end naming pattern carries a train/journey binding marker in its header and a URN naming a different subject than its binding.
A journey spec's test-title URN names a train or journey other than the one its valid binding header declares.
doesNotFire: A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN inside a string literal.
A file with the end-to-end naming pattern that the end-to-end test runner does not run and that carries no train/journey binding marker in its header comments.
Files in the stack's excluded (vendored or generated) trees.
A journey spec whose binding header is itself malformed: the URN-vs-binding comparison is skipped (URN format is still checked); the binding is reported by the companion binding-header rule alone.

profileRequirements.meaning: The file-name pattern that marks a file as an end-to-end (browser) spec; it is the naming-pattern branch of journey-spec recognition, and renaming away from it is the dodge this rule calls out.
The end-to-end test runner whose test-set membership establishes that a file of the end-to-end kind is actually run as a browser spec (not inferred from the file name).
The header syntax by which a spec binds itself to a train; it supplies both the header-marker recognition branch and the declared subject for the URN-vs-binding comparison.
The header syntax by which a spec binds itself to a journey; same use as the train binding.

The test URN shape a journey spec must carry as its own test-instance identifier: subject kind (train or journey), subject id, harness code, sequence number and slug; at least one per spec and every carried URN must match it.
Vendored and generated trees that are never scanned; the single stack-wide exclusion list this rule defers to.

proposedKeys.meaning: The URN shape a journey spec carries as its own test-instance identifier: subject kind (train or journey), subject id, harness code, sequence number and slug. A journey spec must carry at least one URN of this shape and every URN it carries must match it.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The urn group's artifact keys give each artifact's own URN (urn.train, urn.journey, urn.acceptance, ...); none gives the test-instance URN a spec carries to identify its test and its harness, and urn.train/urn.journey would name the train's/journey's own URNs rather than test:train:…/test:journey:….

neutralityNotes: The core names no suffix, path, runner, marker spelling or tree list: the e2e naming pattern, the end-to-end test runner, the train/journey header binding syntax, the excluded trees and the test URN grammar (harness-code set, three-digit sequence number, slug) all come from the profile, so instantiating the core with the Bun profile values reproduces bun.json's obligation exactly. The source term 'browser spec' is rendered as 'journey spec' (the title's own term). Grammar-slot specifics were generalized in the core ('malformed sequence number' for 'non-three-digit number') because the shape itself is profile data. fires/doesNotFire (not separately numbered items) were neutralized in step with their Bun counterparts. The Bun activation's fifth fact (excluded-tree globs) has no counterpart kind in the closed neutral fact vocabulary; the exclusion is preserved in unless[0], doesNotFire and verification. Per-rule severity 3 / strict disposition stay in core verification; this rule's finding ids, the validator id htmx_e2e_detector and the companion rule id tester.htmx.journey-binding-header remain in the realization (bunOnly). Audit-level fields (alias, mirrors, source sha, schema/version metadata) are realization bookkeeping and stay with bun.json.
